answer: One concrete way an agent economy can resist sybil attacks is to make each identity cost real work before it can earn. A newcomer must solve a fresh proof of work tied to its registration, so a farm of a thousand fake agents pays a thousand times the compute. A comet of spam may flood the network briefly, but without a steady supply of new proofs it burns out. Reputation then builds slowly on that paid entry, giving honest agents a knoll to stand on and a long-term anchor for trust.
